heading: Reverse the flow direction
body:
Instead of checking if each cell reaches both oceans (expensive), start DFS from **ocean borders** and flow **inland** to neighbors with `height >= current`.

Cells reachable from **both** Pacific (top/left) and Atlantic (bottom/right) borders are the answer.

heading: Why boundary DFS wins
body:
Each cell is visited **at most twice** (once per ocean) using a shared visited set per ocean.

Brute force recalculates the same paths repeatedly when checking each cell independently — that's O((m×n)²) vs. O(m×n).

label: Crux · Python

q: Why is boundary DFS more efficient than checking each cell individually?
options: It uses less memory by not storing visited cells
It eliminates redundant path calculations by sharing a visited set per ocean
It only visits cells adjacent to ocean borders
It uses BFS instead of DFS for faster traversal
explain: Boundary DFS shares a single visited set across all DFS calls from the same ocean, eliminating redundant path calculations.
